title: Tool Calling Is Not Production Readiness

slides.author: Alexey Grigorev
slides.title: Tool calling is only one step
slides.subtitle: Production agents need an execution layer around the function call.

slides.title: A schema is not a workflow
slides.body: Tool calling means the agent can call a function with structured arguments. It does not answer what happens when the call fails.

slides.title: The retry question
slides.body: If a support ticket request times out, should the workflow retry? If the ticket was created, a blind retry can create a duplicate.

slides.title: Production needs history
slides.body: The workflow needs to know what was attempted, what failed, what returned, and whether retrying is safe.

slides.title: Useful details to keep
slides.body: Store per-step inputs, outputs, timeout state, retry count, recovery path, and idempotency information for side effects.

slides.title: Workshop focus
slides.body: We will look at state, retries, timeouts, recovery paths, human approval steps, and traces for production agent workflows.

slides.supportingText: Running Durable Agents in Production, June 16, 4:30-6:00 PM GMT+2 on YouTube.
